posts.heading: September 23, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 302 visits across 23 species, exceeding the weekly average of 234.9 visits. Carolina Chickadees, Northern Cardinals, and Tufted Titmice were present, with Tufted Titmice contributing significantly to the high visit count. American Robins, Song Sparrows, and Common Grackles were absent, a contrast to their presence in previous days.

The auditory log recorded 336 detections, exceeding the recent average, with Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinals dominating the counts. An Eastern Screech-Owl was heard for the first time in 14 days. A Tufted Titmouse was observed feeding from a treat bowl.

posts.heading: September 22, 2026
posts.text:
Feeder traffic reached 421 visits, double the recent mean of 213.3. Tufted Titmice accounted for 202 of these visits, while House Finches and Northern Cardinals remained consistent regulars. The species count rose to 23, exceeding the average of 20.1, driven by the return of the Cedar Waxwing, which had been absent since September 15.

Vocal activity totaled 251 detections, below the weekly average of 296.4. Carolina Wrens and Eastern Towhees maintained their usual presence, with the former leading in detection count. Eastern Phoebes, recorded every day in the past week, did not appear, nor did Downy Woodpeckers or White-eyed Vireos.

The day spanned from a Tufted Titmouse seen six minutes before sunrise to a Northern Cardinal seven minutes after sunset.

posts.heading: September 21, 2026
posts.text: The station recorded 124 feeder visits, compared to the recent weekly average of 230. The species count dipped to 18 from the mean of 20. Tufted Titmice were the most frequent visitors, seen 64 times, with Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinals following at 14 and 11 visits respectively. American Crows, Carolina Wrens, and Northern Cardinals provided the bulk of vocal detections. The day concluded with a Tufted Titmouse visiting 21 minutes before sunset, following its arrival 12 minutes before sunrise.
